title: White Flyer Plant Manager
text:
**Title:**
Plant Manager
 
 
**Location**
: Knox, IN
 
 
**Salary:**
$126,000 to $148,200 (depending on relevant experience)
 
 
**Sched**
ule: Onsite, Monday through Friday
 
 
**Websites:**
Winchester.com and WhiteFlyer.com
 
 
**Focus:**
The Plant Manager serves as the leader of the facility, responsible for driving operational excellence and delivering business results through a strong culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement. This role provides strategic direction and day-to-day leadership across all plant operations, ensuring the achievement of key objectives in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee engagement.
 
 
**Plant Manager Essential Job Functions:**

* Lead all aspects of plant operations to achieve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and financial objectives.
* Develop and execute operational strategies that support business goals and long-term growth.
* Manage plant budgets, operating costs, and capital improvement projects.
* Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Lead and develop personnel while fostering a culture of accountability and engagement.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve efficiency, quality, and profitability.
* Monitor key operational and financial performance metrics and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Ensure adequate raw material inventories and supply availability to support uninterrupted production.

**Plant Manager Minimum Requirements:**

* Must meet one of the following:

+ Bachelor’s degree\* in engineering, business administration, supply chain, or finance with three years of relevant supervisory experience.
+ High school diploma or equivalent with nine years of relevant manufacturing supervisory experience.
+ High school diploma or equivalent with fifteen years of clay target manufacturing experience.

* Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to identify root causes and implement corrective actions for manufacturing processes and equipment improvements.
* Experience with the following is preferred:

+ Optimization of supply chains and manufacturing processes.
+ Inventory management and supply and demand balancing/planning.

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel; SAP experience preferred.
* Ability to work with Corporate EHS to ensure site compliance with local, state, and federal regulations.
* Excellent analytical, leadership, communication (verbal and written), organizational, presentation, problem-solving, project management, and decision-making skills.
* Demonstrated ability to work independently, establish priorities, manage multiple responsibilities, adapt to changing business demands, and collaborate effectively across teams.
* Valid driver's license required.
* Ability to travel up to 5-10%.

**Physical and work Environment Requirements:**

* This position requires access to ITAR controlled technical data, and as such, employment will be contingent upon the candidate's ability to access ITAR controlled technical data pursuant to an export license approved by the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls, if required.
* This role is approximately 60% office-based and 40% plant-based with allocation varying based on operational requirements and business needs
* The position requires the ability to safely access and navigate an operating industrial facility, and requires the ability to walk, work, and stand on various surface conditions for extended periods of time, including asphalt, rock, gravel, uneven terrain, metal grating, and metal plate overlays; as well as climb stairs, ladders, and access elevated platforms throughout site units
* This role includes exposure to outdoor conditions, including varying temperatures, heat, and humidity during site inspections and field activities
* The role requires use of appropriate PPE, including hard hat, safety glasses, flame-resistant clothing, respirator, and steel-toe boots
* Essential functions must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation, consistent with applicable law and safety requirements

**Strong Careers Grow Here**
Rooted in our corporate values , Olin continues to be the global leader in both ammunition and chemical manufacturing. We invest, recognize, and reward the talents and contributions of our employees, empowering over 8,000 global individuals to make an impact both at work and in surrounding communities.
 
 
Olin fosters a diverse and inclusive workplace, where you are encouraged to join or lead our Olin People Networks. These voluntary groups connect employees across sites, divisions and functions to strengthen connections, belonging, and community involvement. View a snapshot of our comprehensive benefits package.
 
 

* Degree must be from a school that is accredited by an accrediting agency recognized by the Secretary of Education of the U.S. Department of Education or equivalent program from an international university.

Olin does not provide any form of sponsorship. We will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F-1, H-1, H-2, L, B, J or TN or who need sponsorship now or in the future, are not eligible for hire.
 
 
**Olin is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.**
